title: Chapter 42 — The Custom Builder
intro: The trade book's anchor account — how custom builders work and the service model that wins a decade.

sections.title: How Custom Builders Work
sections.content:
Custom builders are building one-of-a-kind homes for clients who have specific expectations and significant budgets. The appliance package is a line item on a project that might cost $500,000 to $5,000,000.

They need you to provide spec packages at three price tiers. They need you to coordinate with their trades — electricians, plumbers, cabinetmakers. They need you to deliver to a construction site on a specific day during a specific phase. And they need you to handle warranty issues so their client never calls them about an appliance problem.

sections.title: Winning the Account
sections.content:
Visit their job site or office. Do not wait for them to come to you. Bring a spec package: your top three appliance packages at three price tiers with photos, specs, and delivered pricing. Offer to do a walk-through of a model home and recommend the appliance package.

Provide one contact — you — for everything: quotes, changes, delivery coordination, warranty issues. Follow through relentlessly. One missed delivery on a builder job and you lose the account.

The spec meeting is where you earn or lose the account. Include installation requirements so their trades know what to rough in.

sections.title: The Decade Relationship
sections.content:
A custom builder who trusts you will use you for every home they build for the next decade. That is 20-50 homes. At $8,000-$15,000 per home in appliances, that single relationship is worth $160,000-$750,000 over ten years.

This is why you never miss a delivery date. Never misquote a spec. Never let a warranty issue go unresolved. The stakes on every interaction are not one sale — they are a decade of sales.
